issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() as a no-argument method returning an int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) with a boolean parameter. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected method signature and will prevent their implementation (following the specification) from matching the solution's API.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem specification by changing the solution method signature to public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() (no parameters) and have it return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents. Update any internal calls (e.g. getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) to call the no-arg version. Alternatively, if the boolean parameter was intended, update the problem statement and UML to declare getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests): int.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and task description) defines a method getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This changes the method signature (and expected usage) and creates a mapping confusion: students will look for a no-arg getTotalNumberOfStudents() as specified by the exercise and tests, while the solution provides a boolean-parameter variant.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the problem specification: change the solution method signature to public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() (no parameters) and implement the intended behavior (e.g., include guest students by default or provide a separate overloaded method if needed). Alternatively, update the problem/UML to document the boolean parameter if that variation is intentional, but keep both artifacts consistent.
